name: Kurosawa Genzō

answers.ninjo: He wants to believe the next captain who hires him won't eventually ask him to do something that makes him run again.
answers.standout_quality: He accepts jobs that keep him moving and solvent, but turns down the ones that would require him to stay in one place long enough to form attachments.
answers.accomplishment: He followed a merchant captain's runaway daughter three days upriver through fog and fouled current to a shrine town, and brought her back without the captain ever learning she had gone.
answers.challenge: When a captain asks him to stay through winter to train the crew, Genzō finds himself caught between the steady work that would let him stop running and the certainty that staying means eventually being asked to do something unforgivable.
answers.peace: He stands at the river's edge before dawn with a bow he has never named, drawing and releasing until his shoulders burn and the strife drains from his chest like water through cupped hands.
answers.fear: When a younger swordsman bests him in a sparring match before the crew, Genzō finds himself accepting the captain's offer to stay through winter, teaching the boy everything he knows, each lesson a small wound he cannot stop reopening.
answers.past: He deserted his lord's service after witnessing the man order the execution of a fishing village that had sheltered enemy refugees, and he has been running jobs for merchant captains ever since rather than risk serving anyone who might ask him to do it again.
answers.known_for: The merchant captains in the River ports know he will cut a man down without hesitation, but they have never seen him take a job that would keep him docked longer than the hull needs caulking.
answers.prized_possession: The bowstring he braids from horsehair each winter is shorter than it should be, frayed where he has retied it a dozen times rather than replace it, because the bow itself came from Mirumoto Yoshitô and he cannot afford to know whether a new string would shoot true.
answers.group_history: Michio watches Genzō turn down a winter posting that would have paid enough to stop running, then accepts the same captain's offer three days later when the boy who beat him in sparring asks for instruction.
answers.raised_by: A merchant captain's widow raised him from fourteen after his parents drowned in a river accident, and he still cannot refuse work that takes him away from her port for more than a season.
answers.stress_reaction: When the pressure mounts and he cannot leave, Genzō's hands move to his bowstring—checking the fraying, retying the knots, running his thumb along the horsehair until his fingers bleed.
answers.relationships:
Michio (Nezumi Tattered Ear Explorer Tradition) — Michio brings him work that moves upriver, and Genzō accepts every job without asking questions, though he watches the Nezumi's face to see if this one will be the kind that keeps him still.
Mirumoto Manami (Dragon) — Mirumoto Manami trained him in the forms after he fled his lord's service, and he has not spoken to her in three years because she keeps sending letters asking him to come home to the Dragon.

bio:
Kurosawa Genzō is a deserter-turned-rōnin duelist, wandering the land and offering his sword to whoever can meet his price. Though he carries himself with the discipline of a samurai, he no longer claims the title, instead forging his own sense of honor. He avoids pointless fights, only drawing his blade when there is purpose behind it.

His scarred, battle-hardened face still carries boyish charm, though he maintains a gruff default demeanor to keep others at a distance. He struggles to trust others, fearing betrayal or obligation, and regrets abandoning his duty, wondering if he can ever reclaim his lost honor. He sharpens his blade to find peace, a steady ritual that reminds him that he is still in control of his fate.

Genzō once spared a defeated opponent who later repaid the debt, reinforcing his belief that honor is found in action, not station. However, he knows that one wrong move could lead to an ignominious death, a fate he refuses to accept. Though he gambles on fights, he does not gamble with his own survival — he has lived this long, and he does not intend to die easily.
